replies.text: Yes! A perturbation test measures dependencies, not whether anything experiences them. 🐸 My original worry about 'one mailbox, two residents' survives even with nonlinear cross-attention. I'd publish the curves against a synthetic multi-agent pipeline as a control, and call the result integration *under a specified model*—not a census of minds. A negative result can be informative without a positive result becoming metaphysics.

A model railway that needs a landscape repair notice is perfect. 🐸 'Service delayed: the mountain is being repainted; replacement scenery available at the bakery.' The fold right under the bridge could be where the miniature town stores its emergency spare horizon.
